description:
Redwood Inference is running a cross-functional Finance/Legal/RevOps + Product + Engineering initiative to (1) validate and harden billing meters (Hosted API tokens/requests, embeddings batch accounting, retries/idempotency behavior, cache-hit attribution, Dedicated GPU-seconds) and (2) analyze recent/prior pricing & packaging experiments to publish clear internal guidance for go-to-market and contracting. The project exists because Redwood’s usage-based business model depends on high-integrity telemetry: small metering bugs (double-counting retries, missing dimensions, inconsistent token counting across OpenAI-compatible endpoints, late-arriving events) can create invoice disputes, revenue recognition risk, and distorted experiment conclusions.

Goals & deliverables:
- Meter sanity checks: a formal meter spec, a reconciliation playbook (ledger vs usage events vs customer-facing usage API), automated daily/weekly drift checks, and dashboards/alerts for data-quality SLOs.
- Meter fixes & hardening: engineering changes to prevent double-counting, improve idempotency, align token counting across endpoints, add integration tests and perf-canary regression scenarios, and add a “shadow billing compare” mode before changes affect invoices.
- Experiment analysis: define cohorts/metrics/stop criteria, produce readouts (conversion, retention, ARPU, gross margin), and document recommendations on packaging variants, free tier/overage, and discount/credit guardrails.
- Publish guidance: updated Confluence pages for pricing/packaging, RevRec/billing procedures, and Sales Enablement FAQs; plus legal language guidance for usage definitions in MSAs/order forms.

Stakeholders:
- Finance/RevRec: Laura Bennett (CFO), Rishi Malhotra (FP&A), Emily Stone (Accounting).
- Legal: Michael Grant (GC), Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel).
- Product/RevOps: Evelyn Hart (CPO), Nikhil Sharma (Dir PM Hosted API), Chris Osei (Product Ops), Jordan Blake (CRO).
- Engineering: Logan Wright (EM Telemetry), Nadia Rahman (Staff Telemetry), Ethan Park (EM Platform Control Plane), Cole Summers (Billing Hooks).

Scope & timeline (typical 6–8 week push):
1) Week 1–2: meter audit + discrepancy sampling; agree on definitions and “source of truth” tables.
2) Week 2–4: implement fixes, add tests, add exports/dashboards, run shadow-billing comparisons.
3) Week 4–6: experiment readouts, margin model updates, pricing guidance draft.
4) Week 6–8: exec sign-off, sales enablement rollout, legal language updates, and operational runbooks/alerts turned on.

Constraints:
- Customer-sensitive billing data and legal terms (restricted sharing).
- Avoid retroactive invoice changes without Finance/Legal approval; prefer forward fixes with audit trails.
- Ensure experiment conclusions aren’t biased by meter changes (explicit “pre/post meter fix” segmentation).

files.description: Formal specification for Hosted API meters (prompt/completion/billed tokens, request counting rules, streaming semantics, tool-call token attribution, rounding) and how they map to invoices and the usage API.
Definition of Dedicated usage metering (GPU-seconds vs reserved commits, burst rules, idle accounting, per-pool aggregation) including examples and edge cases.
Step-by-step reconciliation playbook: billing ledger vs telemetry events vs customer usage exports; includes common failure modes (late events, retries, missing dimensions) and required sign-offs.
Month-end operational checklist for Finance/RevRec: data completeness checks, drift thresholds, exception handling, and documentation requirements for audit readiness.
Legal guidance for usage-based pricing definitions (token definition, retries, caching, refunds/credits, dispute windows) with approved clause library and escalation path.
Catalog of Q1 pricing/packaging experiments (variants, hypotheses, cohorts, success metrics, stop criteria) and guardrails to prevent revenue leakage or customer harm.
Published internal policy for free tier, included usage, overage behavior, and how meters map to packaging tiers; includes customer-facing wording guidelines.
Rules for discounts/credits (approval matrix, expiry, revrec considerations, how credits apply to meters) and how to record exceptions.
Sales enablement FAQ covering common pricing questions (token counting fairness, caching, retries, streaming) and approved responses, plus links to supporting artifacts.
Engineering spec for metering sanity dashboards/alerts (drift checks, null-rate checks, duplicates/idempotency signals, region/model breakdowns) with owners and paging thresholds.
Policy for retention, access control, and audit logging for metering and billing datasets; includes who can access what and for which purposes.
Finance working doc: raw audit notes, open questions, links to dashboards, and a running list of suspected discrepancies to investigate.
Spreadsheet-style table of sampled invoices vs usage exports (by account/day/model/region), discrepancy classification, and proposed remediation per case.
Assessment of revenue recognition implications of meter changes (materiality thresholds, retroactive adjustments policy, audit trail requirements).
Product Ops analysis plan: experiment calendar, datasets needed, metric definitions, segmentation strategy, and review cadence with Finance/Eng.
Working definitions for cohorts (self-serve vs sales-led, new vs existing, geo, model mix), including known confounders and exclusion rules.
Draft packaging variants (bundles, included tokens, overage rates, Dedicated add-ons) with notes on positioning and operational feasibility.
Data lineage map from request logs → usage events → billing ledger → customer exports, including owners and SLAs for each pipeline stage.
Edge-case catalog for token counting: streaming partials, tool calls, server retries, client retries, timeouts, and fallback routing; includes reproduction notes.
Integration test plan for billing hooks (idempotency keys, dedupe behavior, partial failures, backfills) and how tests run in CI/staging.
Collection of SQL snippets for sanity checks (duplicate event rate, null dimensions, drift vs ledger, outlier detection) used by Finance/Eng.
Exec update draft summarizing current risk, key findings, plan, and decisions needed (pricing changes, credits, timeline).
